title: Lining up for a photo: counting arrangements
examples: How many ways can 4 people line up?
Why do you multiply when counting arrangements?

explain.say: Four friends, Aiko, Bayo, Carlos and Divya, want a photo in a row. How many different line-ups are there? Let us fill the places one by one. Look at the first stage: anyone can stand first, so there are 4 choices.

explain.say: Someone is now in first place, so 3 friends are left for second place. See the second stage? For each of the 4 first choices there are 3 second choices: 4 times 3 is 12 so far.

stages.label: 1st place: 4 choices

stages.label: 4th place: 1 left
stages.note: The last friend has no choice.

explain.say: Third place: only 2 friends left to choose from. Look at the third stage. 12 times 2 is 24. How many choices are left for the last place?

stages.label: 1st place: 4 choices
stages.ask: Why do you multiply when counting arrangements?

stages.label: 4th place: 1 left

explain.say: Just 1! The last friend fills the last spot. Look at the fourth stage. So the total is 4 times 3 times 2 times 1, which is 24 line-ups. We multiply because every choice can be paired with every later choice.

stages.label: 1st place: 4 choices
stages.ask: Why do you multiply when counting arrangements?

stages.label: 4th place: 1 left

explain.say: Well done! 4 times 3 times 2 times 1 is written 4 factorial, 4 with an exclamation mark. Wow fact: a class of 25 can line up in about 15 million billion billion ways, far more than grains of sand on Earth.

faq.q: Why do you multiply when counting arrangements?
faq.a: Each first choice can go with each second choice, and so on. For 4 first choices and 3 second choices, that makes 4 groups of 3, so 12. Multiplying counts all the combinations of choices.
4 factorial, written 4!, means 4 times 3 times 2 times 1, which is 24. It counts the ways to arrange 4 different things in a row.

faq.q: How many ways can 4 people line up?
faq.a: 24 ways: 4 choices for first, 3 for second, 2 for third and 1 for last.

faq.q: How many ways can you choose a first, second and third from 10 runners?
faq.a: 10 times 9 times 8, which is 720. You stop after three places.
asks: How many ways to award gold, silver and bronze?

faq.a: 0 factorial is defined as 1: there is exactly one way to arrange nothing. This keeps the formulas working.

quiz.say: How many ways can 5 books be arranged on a shelf?
quiz.show: How many ways can 5 books be arranged on a shelf?

wrong.0: 25 is 5 × 5, but you cannot use the same book twice.

quiz.say: In how many ways can gold, silver and bronze go to 8 runners?
quiz.show: In how many ways can gold, silver and bronze go to 8 runners?

wrong.2: 512 is 8 × 8 × 8, letting one runner win two medals.
